q-165868.name: Question 1
q-165868.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the double-angle formula for the hyperbolic sine:

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡x(1-4\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-4\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-2\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

cosh⁡x−cosh⁡2x+C
b

First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine:

sin⁡2x=2sin⁡xcos⁡x

sinh⁡2x=2sinh⁡xcosh⁡x

∫sinh⁡x(1−4cosh⁡x)dx=∫(sinh⁡x−4sinh⁡xcosh⁡x)dx=∫(sinh⁡x−2sinh⁡2x)dx=cosh⁡x−cosh⁡2x+C.

q-97002.name: Question 2
q-97002.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta 
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the double-angle formula for the hyperbolic sine:

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sinh}⁡\theta \operatorname{cosh}⁡\theta 
$$

 

Letting $\theta =3x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sinh}⁡6x=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡3x\operatorname{cosh}⁡3x\,⇒\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡6x=\operatorname{sinh}⁡3x\operatorname{cosh}⁡3x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4\operatorname{sinh}⁡3x\operatorname{cosh}⁡3x\,\text{d}x & =4\int \frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡6x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡6x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{6}\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

q-95871.name: Question 4
q-95871.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the double-angle formula for the hyperbolic sine:

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x
$$

Rearranging the above formula, we get

$$
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int 6\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 3\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+C \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}

q-96997.name: Question 5
q-96997.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the double-angle formula for the hyperbolic sine:

$$
\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x
$$

Rearranging the above formula, we get

$$
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡x(2+3\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+3\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+3\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x+\frac{3}{2}\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x+\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+C \\  & =2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x+\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97017.name: Question 6
q-97017.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta ={cosh}^{2}⁡\theta +{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =2x,$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x={cosh}^{2}⁡2x+{sinh}^{2}⁡2x.
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2{cosh}^{2}⁡2x+2{sinh}^{2}⁡4x)\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }({cosh}^{2}⁡2x+{sinh}^{2}⁡4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡4x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡4\pi -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡x={cosh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+{sinh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).

q-165874.name: Question 8
q-165874.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta ={cosh}^{2}⁡\theta +{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =3x,$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x={cosh}^{2}⁡3x+{sinh}^{2}⁡3x.
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2{sinh}^{2}⁡3x+2{cosh}^{2}⁡3x-1)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}(2({cosh}^{2}⁡3x+{sinh}^{2}⁡3x)-1)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}(2\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sinh}⁡6x-x){|}_{0}^{1/3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2-\frac{1}{3}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡2-1).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

q-95873.name: Question 10
q-95873.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x={cosh}^{2}⁡x+{sinh}^{2}⁡x
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3{cosh}^{2}⁡x+3{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int 3({cosh}^{2}⁡x+{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int ({cosh}^{2}⁡x+{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+C \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95876.name: Question 11
q-95876.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta =2{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =2x$, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡2x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$

q-351902.name: Question 15
q-351902.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta =2{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =x$, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}({cosh}^{2}⁡x+3)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+1)+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+\frac{7}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+\frac{7}{2}x)|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}]-[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sinh}⁡0+0] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\pi )+\frac{7\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-352425.name: Question 16
q-352425.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x=1+2{sinh}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
{sinh}^{2}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x-1).
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(2-12{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[2-12\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x-1)]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(8-6\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(8x-3\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x)\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =[8\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡3)]-[0-0] \\  & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3(\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-{e}^{-2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}}{2}) \\  & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡3-3(\frac{{3}^{2}-{3}^{-2}}{2}) \\  & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\frac{40}{3}\end{aligned}

q-97073.name: Question 17
q-97073.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta =1+2{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta -1).
$$

Letting $\theta =2x$, we have

$$
{sinh}^{2}⁡2x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x-1).
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4{sinh}^{2}⁡2x+3)\,\text{d}x & =\int (4\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x-1)+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sinh}⁡4x+x+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡4x+x+C\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine:

cos⁡2x=1−2sin2⁡x

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

cosh⁡2x=1+2sinh2⁡x

We can rearrange the above formula as

sinh2⁡x=12(cosh⁡2x−1).
